content: LLMs generating tests/oracles are prone to hallucination, producing syntactically valid but logically flawed tests based on incorrect assumptions about intended behavior. A common failure pattern: the LLM aligns expected values to whatever the code under test currently outputs, producing tests that pass trivially without validating intended functionality (defeats the purpose of regression testing). Mitigations in research: multi-agent reflection/re-think passes that re-evaluate generated tests against requirements before accepting them, and few-shot examples distinguishing true failures from false positives.
